title: Reteach on flat gain, not low accuracy
statement: Reteach when a learner's gain is flat, not merely when accuracy is low.
detail: An assessment-quality memo for a reading course sets out the platform's adaptive policy: positive gain short of the cut keeps a learner practising on fresh items, and only flat learning gain routes to reteaching, with recovery checked on a different slice of evidence, never the same items; gaming is treated as distinct from misunderstanding (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-2/approval-package-v2/sources/ASSESSMENT-QUALITY-MEMO.md`). An assessment BrainLift in the course plans' feedback folder sets the same stopping policy: stop early when evidence is decisive, gather more when it is ambiguous, and change approach when learning gain is flat (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`). Meet rapid guessing and hint abuse with an integrity response, not reteaching.
against: The course that wrote the memo does not drive the adaptive engine, so flat-gain detection is outside its scope and nothing there measures it (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-2/approval-package-v2/sources/ASSESSMENT-QUALITY-MEMO.md`, §6).

evidence.quote: The load-bearing signal is **flat gain, not low accuracy**
rapid-guessing and help-abuse get an integrity response, not reteaching.
When evidence is decisive, stop early; when ambiguous, gather more; when flat learning gain, change approach.
And **gaming ≠ misunderstanding** (#32): rapid-guessing and help-abuse get an integrity response, not reteaching.

(0 of 432 built items have a `difficulty` field). Without difficulty/discrimination metadata the adaptive loop flat-lines at "medium," so *flat-gain detection cannot yet be computed the way this policy requires*.
